acceptanceCriteria: The cause of the portable consumer's UNSUPPORTED answer on hosted macos-15 is identified from its own diagnostic output (retained), not inferred
The TCB-V0 gate and portable tests pass on a hosted macos-15 run (run id retained) without skipping, masking or relaxing the verifier-disagreement refusal

When the portable route is genuinely unsupported on a host, the gate still refuses truthfully and a test proves the refusal names the unsupported route rather than a disagreement, or the AC records why disagreement is the correct code
body: Observed in release-gates nightly run 38559681509 job 115837380242 (macos-15, full-gate, schedule, head 8803b7ddc5d1c4c91affc4102e684cc432bad439, Go 1.27.2, 2026-10-14). internal/taskman TestTCBV0010/0011/0012/0013/0017 (x2)/0018 (cem_verdict_gate_unix_test.go, cem_verdict_portable_unix_test.go) and cmd/corvint TestTCBV0016GateVerdictRunsBothConsumers (cem_gate_verdict_test.go:91) fail: the gate result has code CEM_VERDICT_VERIFIER_DISAGREEMENT, reason verifier-disagreement, native verdict ACCEPT/complete/EXACT, portable {outcome:UNSUPPORTED, route:verify-stable-canonical, verdictSha256 6f625eaf...}. Expected: the portable consumer recomputes the same verdict (grant) or each test's specific refusal (stable-not-accepted, tier-below-anchored). The same tests pass locally on darwin at d63c1c3a1 (go test -run 'TestTCBV001[0-7]' ./internal/taskman, 28 s), so the difference is a hosted-runner environment input to the portable route (suspected: a tool, sandbox or path the interop consumer needs that macos-15 lacks or answers differently), not yet identified. Related: V1-1358 (verify-stable-canonical darwin-only; PR #881) and V1-1282. Earlier nightlies (10-09..10-13) failed on different tests. Blocks a green release-gates nightly for 1.0.0-rc.3. Raw log retained in the orchestrator scratch nightly/115837380242.log.
title: TCB-V0 cem-verdict gate tests fail on hosted macos-15: portable consumer answers UNSUPPORTED (verify-stable-canonical), so every fixture refuses VERIFIER_DISAGREEMENT
